title: Impact of FDA Drug Approval on Biotech Company Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event Study using the market model
- Why: FDA approval dates are well-defined, firm-specific information shocks. An event study around the announcement isolates immediate market reactions. Abnormal returns are computed relative to predicted returns from the market model.
- Key assumptions:
  - Conditional on the market factor (and a short-run firm-specific alpha), expected abnormal returns would be zero absent the approval (no-confounding-events in the short window).
  - The market model parameters are stable over the short horizon, and the event is not anticipated beyond the pre-event window used to estimate alpha.
  - Cross-sectional independence (or at least weak dependence) of firm-level abnormal returns when testing the average CAR.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load packages
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
})

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s63_data.csv"
df <- readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Basic checks
stopifnot(all(c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta") %in% names(df)))

# Ensure types
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    stock_id = as.integer(stock_id),
    event_day = as.integer(event_day),
    ret = as.numeric(ret),
    mkt_ret = as.numeric(mkt_ret),
    beta = as.numeric(beta)
  ) %>%
  filter(is.finite(ret), is.finite(mkt_ret), is.finite(beta))

# 2) Estimate firm-level alpha using pre-event window [-10, -1]
estimate_alpha <- function(d, pre_window = c(-10, -1), min_obs = 3) {
  d %>%
    filter(event_day >= pre_window[1], event_day <= pre_window[2]) %>%
    mutate(ar0 = ret - beta * mkt_ret) %>%
    summarise(
      alpha_hat = if (sum(is.finite(ar0)) >= min_obs) mean(ar0, na.rm = TRUE) else 0,
      n_pre = sum(is.finite(ar0))
    )
}

alphas <- df %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  group_modify(~estimate_alpha(.x)) %>%
  ungroup()

df_mm <- df %>%
  left_join(alphas, by = "stock_id") %>%
  mutate(
    AR_mm = ret - alpha_hat - beta * mkt_ret,   # Market model AR with estimated alpha
    AR_capm0 = ret - beta * mkt_ret,            # CAPM with zero alpha
    AR_ma = ret - mkt_ret                        # Market-adjusted AR
  )

# Helper: compute CAR summary for given AR column and window
compute_car_summary <- function(d, ar_col = "AR_mm", window = c(-1, 1)) {
  req_days <- seq(window[1], window[2])
  car_df <- d %>%
    filter(event_day %in% req_days) %>%
    select(stock_id, event_day, !!sym(ar_col)) %>%
    group_by(stock_id) %>%
    # Keep firms only if they have all required event days
    filter(n_distinct(event_day) == length(req_days)) %>%
    summarise(CAR = sum(!!sym(ar_col)), .groups = "drop")

  n <- nrow(car_df)
  mean_car <- mean(car_df$CAR, na.rm = TRUE)
  sd_car <- sd(car_df$CAR, na.rm = TRUE)
  se <- sd_car / sqrt(n)
  tstat <- if (n > 1 && se > 0) mean_car / se else NA_real_
  pval <- if (n > 1 && se > 0) 2 * pt(-abs(tstat), df = n - 1) else NA_real_
  ci_low <- if (n > 1 && se > 0) mean_car + qt(0.025, df = n - 1) * se else NA_real_
  ci_high <- if (n > 1 && se > 0) mean_car + qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * se else NA_real_

  list(
    window = paste0("[", window[1], ",", window[2], "]"),
    ar_model = ar_col,
    n_firms = n,
    mean_CAR = mean_car,
    t_stat = tstat,
    p_value = pval,
    ci_95 = c(ci_low, ci_high)
  )
}

print_car <- function(res, label = "Estimate") {
  cat(sprintf("%s | Window %s | Model %s\n", label, res$window, res$ar_model))
  cat(sprintf("Firms used: %d\n", res$n_firms))
  cat(sprintf("Average CAR: %.4f\n", res$mean_CAR))
  cat(sprintf("t-stat: %.2f | p-value: %.4f\n", res$t_stat, res$p_value))
  cat(sprintf("95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n\n", res$ci_95[1], res$ci_95[2]))
}

# 3) Main result: Market model CAR over [-1, +1]
main_res <- compute_car_summary(df_mm, ar_col = "AR_mm", window = c(-1, 1))
cat("Main Result: Average CAR around FDA approval (market model with pre-estimated alpha)\n")
print_car(main_res, "Main")

# Additional informative metric: AAR on event day 0
aar_day0 <- df_mm %>%
  filter(event_day == 0) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(is.finite(AR_mm)),
    mean_AAR = mean(AR_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_AAR = sd(AR_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    se = sd_AAR / sqrt(n),
    t = mean_AAR / se,
    p = 2 * pt(-abs(t), df = n - 1)
  )
cat("Event-day abnormal return (AAR) using market model:\n")
with(aar_day0, {
  cat(sprintf("Firms used: %d\n", n))
  cat(sprintf("AAR (day 0): %.4f | t-stat: %.2f | p-value: %.4f\n\n", mean_AAR, t, p))
})

# 4) Robustness checks

# 4a) Alternative event windows with market model
rob_mm_01 <- compute_car_summary(df_mm, ar_col = "AR_mm", window = c(0, 1))
rob_mm_02 <- compute_car_summary(df_mm, ar_col = "AR_mm", window = c(0, 2))
print_car(rob_mm_01, "Robustness (window 0 to +1)")
print_car(rob_mm_02, "Robustness (window 0 to +2)")

# 4b) Alternative AR models, same main window [-1, +1]
rob_capm0 <- compute_car_summary(df_mm, ar_col = "AR_capm0", window = c(-1, 1))
rob_ma    <- compute_car_summary(df_mm, ar_col = "AR_ma", window = c(-1, 1))
print_car(rob_capm0, "Robustness (CAPM alpha=0)")
print_car(rob_ma,    "Robustness (Market-adjusted)")

# 4c) Placebo window in the pre-period (e.g., [-6, -4]) using market model
placebo <- compute_car_summary(df_mm, ar_col = "AR_mm", window = c(-6, -4))
print_car(placebo, "Placebo (pre-event -6 to -4)")

# 5) Report diagnostics for alpha estimation
alpha_diag <- alphas %>%
  summarise(
    firms = n(),
    mean_alpha = mean(alpha_hat, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_alpha = sd(alpha_hat, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_n_pre = mean(n_pre, na.rm = TRUE),
    med_n_pre = median(n_pre, na.rm = TRUE),
    pctl10_n_pre = quantile(n_pre, 0.10, na.rm = TRUE),
    pctl90_n_pre = quantile(n_pre, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

cat("Alpha estimation diagnostics (pre-window [-10, -1]):\n")
cat(sprintf("Firms: %d | Mean alpha: %.5f | SD alpha: %.5f\n", alpha_diag$firms, alpha_diag$mean_alpha, alpha_diag$sd_alpha))
cat(sprintf("Pre-window obs per firm (mean/median/p10/p90): %.1f / %.1f / %.0f / %.0f\n",
            alpha_diag$mean_n_pre, alpha_diag$med_n_pre, alpha_diag$pctl10_n_pre, alpha_diag$pctl90_n_pre))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. FDA approvals are major positive information shocks for biotech firms; prices should jump on or immediately around day 0.
- Magnitude: For [-1, +1] CAR, I expect roughly +4% to +10% on average, with a sizable day-0 AAR (about +3% to +7%). Larger moves are possible for single-product biotechs; averaging across 60 firms should moderate the effect but remain economically and statistically significant.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Exploit the timing of FDA drug approval announcements as a natural experiment.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: FDA drug approvals lead to a positive change in biotech companies' CAR.
